bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert a Software Engineer Salary Melbourne Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

When researching a **software engineer salary Melbourne**, you will often see figures from job ads or recruiter surveys. For example, SEEK data suggests a typical salary of around $105,000 for a Software Developer in Melbourne. However, the most reliable benchmark for full-time adult ordinary time earnings is the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings, which for May 2026 stands at $2,083.70 per week. That equates to roughly $108,352 annually. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission set the legal minimums, not the market averages.

This guide explains how to convert any hourly rate – whether it's the National Minimum Wage, an award rate, or a market salary – into an annual figure, a fortnightly amount, and an estimate of your take-home pay after tax and Medicare. We assume a standard 38-hour week unless stated otherwise.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52.

Example: If your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

For a fortnightly figure, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Using the same example, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement.

**Award rates** are higher minimums for specific industries. For example, the Clerks—Private Sector Award 2020 (MA000002) sets minimum hourly rates from $26.97 for Level 1 Year 1 up to $37.24 for a call centre technical associate. Software engineers are often covered by the Professional Employees Award 2020, which has its own classification rates. Always check the relevant award via the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

**Casual loading** is an extra 25% on the minimum hourly rate, paid instead of entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. If you are a casual employee, your base rate is the award or minimum rate, and the loading is added on top. Our [timesheet](/about) includes a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading automatically.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This does not reduce your take-home pay – it is an additional benefit. The super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a software engineer salary Melbourne of $108,352, the super contribution would be $13,002.24 per year, bringing total remuneration to $121,354.24.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

Example: For an annual gross of $59,280 (from $30/hour):
- Tax: $0 on first $18,200; 15% on $26,800 = $4,020; 30% on $14,280 = $4,284; total tax = $8,304.
- Medicare: 2% of $59,280 = $1,185.60.
- Net annual pay = $59,280 - $8,304 - $1,185.60 = $49,790.40.
- Fortnightly net = $49,790.40 / 26 = $1,915.02.

### Using the Calculator

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are casual, tick the box to add the 25% loading. The calculator then shows your annual gross, fortnightly gross, estimated tax, Medicare, and net pay. It also displays the super contribution paid on top.

For a **software engineer salary Melbourne**, if you earn $50 per hour (a common rate for experienced engineers), your annual gross would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. After tax and Medicare, your net annual pay would be approximately $73,000, or $2,807 per fortnight. Your employer would also pay $11,856 in super.

### Important Notes and Limitations

- The calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed.
- HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

Always consult the [reference tables](/data) for the latest award rates and the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the National Minimum Wage updates.

### Summary

Whether you are a job seeker comparing a **software engineer salary Melbourne** offer, or an employer setting pay rates, the formula is straightforward: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides for your award, and use the ABS for average earnings to benchmark your market value. The calculator on this site gives you a reliable estimate of your annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay.
